exercise1.prompt: A Book class with title and author as instance variables

cases.name: the book keeps the title it was made with
prints the title and the author
Book is a class with an __init__
cases.describe: a Book class whose __init__ takes a title and an author

hiddenCases.name: a different book gets its own title
a different book gets its own author

exercise1.hint: Instance variables are set on self inside __init__, from the parameters. Values written directly in the class body are shared by every book, which is why a second book with different details catches that mistake.

exercise2.prompt: A BankAccount with a balance, a deposit method and a get_balance method

cases.name: a new account starts at zero
prints the balance after the deposit
deposit and get_balance are methods on the class
cases.describe: a BankAccount class with deposit and get_balance inside it

hiddenCases.name: each account has its own balance

exercise2.hint: deposit has to add to what is already there rather than replace it, so two deposits in a row are what tells the two apart. Both methods go inside the class, each taking self first.

questions.prompt: Where does an instance variable get its value?
choices: From the class body, once, for every object
From self inside a method, separately for each object
From a global variable of the same name
From the name of the class
questions.explain: Anything assigned to self belongs to that one object. That is what makes two books able to have different titles.

questions.prompt: Why does deposit take self as its first parameter?
choices: Python requires every function to have it
So the method can reach the balance of the account it was called on
So the method can be called without an object
questions.explain: account.deposit(100) passes account in as self. Without it the method has no account to add the money to.

questions.prompt: Which lines belong inside the class body, indented under `class BankAccount:`?
questions.explain: The methods are part of the class. Making an account and printing its balance are things the program does with the class, so they sit outside it.

questions.prompt: To add to the balance rather than overwrite it, deposit does self.balance ___ amount.
questions.explain: Writing self.balance = amount throws away everything deposited before, and one deposit is not enough to notice.
